Phillipi Horticultural Area under seige

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Food or housing- the centuries old bread basket of Cape Town is under threat by developers

Summary:
The Philippi Horticultural area – PHA- is a unique farming community of over 3000 hectares producing 200 000 tonnes of vegetables and flowers per year situated in the heart of the Cape Flats, a mere 20km from the centre of Cape Town. Most Capetonians have no idea how abundant and productive it is as they rush down the main roads that surround the area. They also have no idea that many of the vegetables they buy in the supermarkets have come from just a few kilometres down the road.

Established by German immigrant farmers in the 1800s, it has been the bread basket of the city for nearly two centuries. It is situated on top of one of the largest underground aquifers in the world and so has an abundance of water. The temperature is ideal for vegetables, as the cool sea breezes keep soaring summer temperatures at bay. As the drought hits food production around South Africa, Philippi has been left unscathed. People are travelling in from further and further out of town to come and buy vegetables from the PHA.
But the area is under threat from growing pressure from the City to provide houses. Two major sections of the Southern part of the PHA, which is the most productive vegetable growing area, have been rezoned. The future of food security in Cape Town is severely threatened

Further information:
PHA has been threatened for years by illegal dumping, by theft from surrounding informal settlements and by farmers selling land to developers when they had no security that the area would remain zoned as agricultural and were loath to invest in farms without the support of the City.

A small group of farmers is fighting back and asking the City planners some serious questions - how could they rezone Agricultural land as Urban when they did not go through all the correct procedures? How can they threaten food security when thousands of Capetonians depend on their food at a reasonable price because they don’t have to carry the burden of increasing transport costs? How will they be able to farm with houses on their borders, and spraying of crops will become a health issue? With hundreds more people travelling on the borders of the fields the crops will become polluted.

Around the country, water is becoming more scare and farmers are struggling to irrigate their crops: the Cape Flats Aquifer is a free source of irrigation water for farmers and it is also the future potable water for the city of Cape Town. The PHA is a natural soak, every year the winter rains replenish the aquifer and the more development happens, the smaller the soak area becomes. Paving over or silica sand mining in the PHA will destroy the recharge function of the aquifer.

Finally it is also a major source of employment - over 6000 workers, mostly uneducated, rural woman and youth, find work close to their homes and apart from their wages have access to food from the fields for their families.

Food and water security in the heart of the City is under siege and the City’s town planners don’t seem to have calculated the cost of losing this remarkable resource.

The story felt jumbled and its not clear what the focus point is – make it clear that this is about urbanisation affecting agriculture
No clear sense of where we are geographically and the map comes in too late
The argument that the city makes is hard to follow please make it clearer
Start with the stealing of vegetables in the context of a country in drought and the night patrols to introduce us to the area, get you into the story and justify the story nd then say its also under threat from the city.
Tell us at the top where we are, where phillipi is located close to ganglands mannenburg and UCT ad other landmarks
Why is this important to people who are far from cape town?
Highlight the conflict between agriculture and urbanisation
Highlight that there is a nationwide drought and cape town has been spared of this
Clarify that the city has final control and that the issue of getting in rates and taxes from more people is of importance to them
Include properly the visuals of the plans for the developments – at the moment your words on screen conflict too much with the background and we missed it entirely.
Please book another viewing.

Start with the crime
Shorten to 8 or 9 min
We dont need to view again

Press Release:


Philippi Under Threat
The Philippi farming community gives the Cape 200 000 tonnes of vegetables and flowers every year. Only 20 kilometres from the centre of town, Philippi has been Cape Town’s bread basket for nearly 2000 years. Carte Blanche asks: why are the city’s own town planners threatening its survival during one of the most devastating droughts this country has ever seen?


Script:


Nabeel” This guy is a problem in the area he steals vegetables and breaks into the people’s houses last week we caught him and then he got locked up
Script: Night patrols have become the only way Urban farmers in Philippi Horticultural Area can survive. They’re farming slap bang in the middle of gang land - Hanover Park, Manenberg, and Guguletu - filled with hungry unemployed people.
Link “The Philippi horticultural area is just 20 minutes from the centre of Cape Town and despite its fairly urban setting its ideal farm land there is plenty of fresh water it doesn’t suffer from extreme temperatures and is able to produce between 3 and 4 crops every year.
Script: Most Capetoinans are oblivious to this incredible resource - cheap abundant vegetables on their doorstep. As the drought bites hard into food security and prices spiral across the country, in Philippi its business as usual for Johan Terblanche one of the biggest commercial farmers in the area.
Johan “I don’t think there is another place in the world where they can do this, in every super market in Cape Town stuff of Philippi is there I would say about 60 -70% of the stuff people eat every day comes out of Phillip vegetables
Script: But 3000 hectares of zoned agricultural land tucked away on the Cape Flats it’s under threat. The immediate problem is the relentless crime. Nabel Brinkhuis is an emerging vegetable farmer
Nabeel ” I had an order for about 1000 cauliflowers the Monday on the Thursday when I walked in the land the caulis were almost ready when we came in there on the Monday the guys just told me there are no heads in here they stole almost everything”
Script: Cable theft frequently leaves them without power for days on end. When the wind howls through here at 60 km an hour, the crops get sand blasted, and to keep the plants in the ground, it requires constant irrigation. Cables thieves had stuck the previous evening but fortunately the wind wasn’t howling that day.
Johan “ I lose 4.5 hectares of carrots it is 1.5 million rand and on that side there is 18 hectares full but luckily the council is said they will come immediately and repair the cable it’s an expensive problem and its on-going it is not stopping
Script: Emerging farmer Wadea Jappie is an egg producer and without power she can’t feed her hens
Wadea ”If they do steal the cable it is like 2, 3 days that we are without any electricity ..and if they do get fed the 4th or the 3rd day then it takes about 2 or 3 weeks for them to get back into the production it has major finance effects on us
Script: But a much bigger threat hanging over their future is the shrinking agricultural area. The City has moved the urban edge
Link “One of the biggest challenges faced by the PHA is that it is slowly being squeezed by urban development and no better is that demonstrated than on this particular farm to my right lush green cabbages to my left is an area that could soon be home to 1000’s of people
Script: Emerging organic farmer Nazeer Sonday sees it as a battle between food security and greedy developers
Nazeer “Our area is symptomatic of what is happening in the country, you know we have lost about 2 million hectares of high potential agricultural land through mining, urban development and so on and if this continues who is going to grow our food
Script. And Philippi has an abundance of water- a rare commodity in times of drought and climate change
Link “The Cape Flats aquifer of 620 sq kilometres is one of the world’s biggest it provides about 3000 hectares of farm land with quality fresh water basically this entire area is a massive natural sink
Script: The southern section has the best water supply, and so is the most desirable but the farmers are running out of affordable land. Developers are speculating on farm land buying it up cheaply from farmers who are throwing in the towel
Johan ‘A hectare by us is about 4 / 500 000 sometimes to a million rand a hectare and there is no ways you can farm it out to that so that is why you have to lease and be quick when the other farmers is stopping you must be quick to get that land
Script: Desperate for more land he rehabilitated 20 hectares of former sand mine
Johan “20 hectares cost me more than 4 million rand and that is in Philippi ….over 10 or 15 years I hope to get my money back but for a framers if your heart is there you try everything to survive
Script: So Nazeer spends most of his time fighting to protect the PHA
Nazeer “I will have to be an activist in order that I can farm “
Script: There are a number of emerging farmers in Philippi and they have the most to lose. The PHA Food and farming campaign, have been fighting for the last five years to stop two major developments – which combined will be 26 000 houses, a shopping mall, a private prison, and private schools.
Nazeer “This is a very critical land reform issue but it is also an issue that effects the whole city because if we lose this area we lose everything”
Script: Provincial MEC for Agriculture, economic development and Tourism Alan Winde says they have turned down the applications for both developments
Winde ” This is high potential agricultural land the answer is no, very simple. While the city is under huge pressure for development we have other tracks of land specifically we have old military land in the city
Script: This fight has been going on since 2008
Winde “Nobody applies to do a housing development on top of the Mountain because they would bother wasting their money. That is why in my meeting with the City I said, say it publically that this area is going to be protected for agricultural purposes. As soon as people see gaps in a space and of course an open agricultural area is far easier to develop
Link: It’s clear that the provincial administration would like the PHA to remain an agricultural area what isn’t clear is if the City feels the same way it’s against that background that the farmers say that they are not entirely sure who to turn to or even how to participate in the process
Nazeer “The one development is turned down they change the regulations and its going ahead the other development is turned down they change the regulations and its going ahead”
Script: That is because the law changed in 2015 giving the City of Cape Town the sole responsibility for what happens to Philippi explains Johannes van der Merwe Mayco member for Energy, Environment and Spatial planning
Van der Merwe “ The City will definitely look at what are the Province’s reasons as to why it didn’t want to amend the Urban Edge, but in essence the City also has its own channels through which it works to establish the merits of the case, and so take a decision. The City of Cape Town is really not planning to use Philippi’s farming area for a massive development
Script: Nazeer says he is aware of several applications for development that could wipe out one third of the farming area and cost roughly 4000 mostly marginalised women their jobs.
Van der Merwe ‘The Philippi area is more or less 2 600 hectares. We are talking about an application which is currently in process of 472 hectares which partially, or mostly, is in the area where there are sand dunes etc, and another application which is in process of 96 hectares, so the remaining area is still there for agricultural production etc
Script: All agree the greatest demand is housing for the urban poor, there are already 9000 squatters in and around Philippi but this development is for middle class gated communities in which the Developers stand to make huge amounts of money, as does the City.
Winde “If you take a city view a straight city view they are going to say well 500 units rates and taxes or one unit who doesn’t want to pay rates and taxes.
Script: Councillor van der Merwe was clear neither of the developments has received the final approval and that there was still a long road ahead in which the public could participate. But the farmers fear that the PHA is deliberately being neglected so they can argue the land is degraded and development will clean it up
Link: It’s clear that in Philippi lip service is paid to the cities by laws it’s something that the farmers are constantly battling with which why you have illegal is dumping on one side and on the other lush green vegetables
Nazeer “The city and the province has not really enforced any of the bylaws on the province side there are NEMA laws which they can enforce, to take people to court for illegally using the land as dump sites there is a city of Cape Town by law that says they don’t even have to wait if the property owner has been warned it has the right to enter the guys property and clean it up and send him the bill”
Van der Merwe “There isn’t a question that Philippi, when it comes to illegal dumping, is handled more lightly than the rest of the city.
Script. While Nazeer fights the City on behalf of the farmers, Nabeel patrols the farmlands with the neighbourhood watch.
John “Nabeel how organised are the guys stealing the vegetables
Nabeel” They come in on foot and they pack it in big bags and then you will find bakkies coming in later on in the night and some evenings the bakkies are not even able to manage to get everything on the bakkie so the next morning you will still find 3 big bags
Script: But despite the crime they are committed to farming here and think with the massive influx of people it’s about affordable food close to the City
Johan “They build 40 000 houses with kitchens with no food or they leave us and we put food on 40 000 kitchens every day that is their decision
Script: And it’s the emerging farmers that have the most to lose
Wadea “We are first generation farmers and we would love to leave a legacy for our grandchildren and it is frustrating to farm like this.

Most Capetonians have no idea how abundant and productive it is as they rush down the main roads that surround the area. They also have no idea that many of the vegetables they buy in the supermarkets have come from just a few kilometres down the road. Established by German immigrant farmers in the 1800s, it has been the bread basket of the city for nearly two centuries. It is situated on top of one of the largest underground aquifers in the world and so has an abundance of water. The temperature is ideal for vegetables, as the cool sea breezes keep soaring summer temperatures at bay. As the drought hits food production around South Africa, Philippi has been left unscathed. People are travelling in from further and further out of town to come and buy vegetables from the PHA. But the area is under threat from growing pressure from the City to provide houses. Two major sections of the Southern part of the PHA, which is the most productive vegetable growing area, have been rezoned. The future of food security in Cape Town is severely threatened
metadata.Further information: PHA has been threatened for years by illegal dumping, by theft from surrounding informal settlements and by farmers selling land to developers when they had no security that the area would remain zoned as agricultural and were loath to invest in farms without the support of the City. A small group of farmers is fighting back and asking the City planners some serious questions - how could they rezone Agricultural land as Urban when they did not go through all the correct procedures? How can they threaten food security when thousands of Capetonians depend on their food at a reasonable price because they don’t have to carry the burden of increasing transport costs? How will they be able to farm with houses on their borders, and spraying of crops will become a health issue? With hundreds more people travelling on the borders of the fields the crops will become polluted. Around the country, water is becoming more scare and farmers are struggling to irrigate their crops: the Cape Flats Aquifer is a free source of irrigation water for farmers and it is also the future potable water for the city of Cape Town. The PHA is a natural soak, every year the winter rains replenish the aquifer and the more development happens, the smaller the soak area becomes. Paving over or silica sand mining in the PHA will destroy the recharge function of the aquifer. Finally it is also a major source of employment - over 6000 workers, mostly uneducated, rural woman and youth, find work close to their homes and apart from their wages have access to food from the fields for their families. Food and water security in the heart of the City is under siege and the City’s town planners don’t seem to have calculated the cost of losing this remarkable resource.
